items.title: Iranian regime governmental centers (unspecified locations), Iran: A member of Iran’s negotiating team said a draft granting waivers on sanctions targeting Iranian oil exports has been finalized, with the measures expected to be issued soon.
items.description: A member of Iran’s negotiating team said a draft granting waivers on sanctions targeting Iranian oil exports has been finalized, with the measures expected to be issued soon.
items.rawSummary: The U.S.-Iran nuclear talks are in a volatile standoff, with Iran conditioning any progress on an Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon and a ceasefire, while Washington reiterates threats and insists on permanently dismantling Iran’s nuclear program, even as a draft sanctions waiver on oil exports signals economic relief may be advancing.
items.analysis: The U.S.-Iran memorandum of understanding is under acute strain as both sides escalate public demands during the first days of talks in Switzerland. President Pezeshkian insisted Iran will never abandon uranium enrichment, a position the Trump administration publicly rebuked with direct threats, and Iran warned that continued Israeli presence in southern Lebanon would void the deal, linking nuclear negotiations to the Lebanon conflict. Iran later threatened to halt all talks unless Israel fully withdraws and hostilities cease, formally protested Trump’s threats as a breach of the agreement’s no-threat clause, and Al-Mayadeen reported that Tehran is demanding an apology from Trump and an Israeli withdrawal from southern Lebanon as conditions to return. On the U.S. side, UN Ambassador Waltz stated the goal is to keep Iran’s nuclear program permanently destroyed, and Senator Graham explicitly warned that any future Hezbollah attacks on Israel would trigger U.S. strikes on Iran. Despite the brinkmanship, Iran has reportedly not walked away from negotiations, and a member of Iran’s negotiating team said a draft waiving sanctions on Iranian oil exports has been finalized, suggesting economic relief components are advancing even as covert tensions surfaced with a U.S. homeland security report that Iran attempted to smuggle IRGC members into the U.S. with its World Cup delegation.

items.title: Burgenstock, Switzerland, Switzerland: An Iranian official told Reuters that negotiations between Tehran and Washington have stalled but have not ended.
items.description: An Iranian official told Reuters that negotiations between Tehran and Washington have stalled but have not ended.
items.rawSummary: U.S.-Iran negotiations in Burgenstock saw early technical progress and agreements on sanctions relief and frozen assets before stalling after President Trump's threats, though talks have not formally ended.
items.analysis: The U.S.-Iran quadrilateral talks in Burgenstock moved into the first structured technical negotiations in history, as announced by Vice President Vance, before the Iranian delegation walked out in protest over new strike threats from President Trump. Iranian state media called the threats a violation of the June 18 Memorandum of Understanding, and the walkout — which included refusing a photo with Vance — interrupted a process Vance had described as a historical framework, though a diplomat later told Axios that talks were still ongoing. Earlier, Pakistan’s foreign minister reported an agreement to lower enrichment levels of Iran’s highly enriched uranium, but Iran’s Fars News maintained the nuclear file was not on the agenda; Axios clarified that the enrichment reduction framework was already established in the MOU. During the session, a member of Iran’s team said operational steps to release frozen assets were carried out with Qatar, and Iranian media subsequently reported understandings on sanctions relief for oil exports and the release of frozen assets, while Iran conditioned further progress on ending the war in Lebanon and an Iranian official dismissed Trump’s Hormuz threats as a bluff. Later, an Iranian official told Reuters that the negotiations have stalled but have not ended.

items.title: Israel (Jerusalem/Tel Aviv), Israel: Channel 12 reported that Israel is weighing limited pullbacks from parts of southern Lebanon, including Beaufort, though senior officials say no formal U.S. withdrawal request has been received and maintain that staying on the border line is a red line.
items.description: Channel 12 reported that Israel is weighing limited pullbacks from parts of southern Lebanon, including Beaufort, though senior officials say no formal U.S. withdrawal request has been received and maintain that staying on the border line is a red line.
items.rawSummary: Domestic discontent over the Iran war outcome is surging, polls show overwhelming Israeli dissatisfaction, political leaders spar over strategy and Gaza's future, and Israel signals possible limited withdrawals from southern Lebanon while insisting its security red lines remain.
items.analysis: A Times of Israel poll published on June 21 found that 92% of Israelis consider Iran the winner of the recent conflict, with most respondents saying the war weakened long-term security, failed to meet its objectives, and left them dissatisfied. Opposition leader Yair Lapid has sharply criticized Prime Minister Netanyahu's handling of the war, accusing him of failing to secure U.S. strikes on Iran's energy infrastructure, losing American trust, and reducing Israel to the posture of a scolded subordinate. Within the coalition, Finance Minister Smotrich intensified calls for the full conquest of Gaza, advocating military administration and Israeli resettlement, and warning that a Palestinian state would be a greater national-security catastrophe than Iran due to its proximity to population centers. U.S.-Israel relations remain strained: Vice President Vance's criticism of cabinet ministers and implied conditionality of military support continue to reverberate, and a Likud lawmaker publicly discarded a MAGA hat in defiance of Trump. The New York Times reported that U.S. intelligence agencies are skeptical Israel will actually cease military operations in Lebanon despite the ceasefire, while Defense Minister Katz insisted Israel will not withdraw from security zones. Netanyahu later declared Israel will remain in the southern Lebanon security zone as long as necessary and vowed to prevent Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons. Trump's claim that Iran was completely defeated militarily contrasts with the domestic perception of a strategic setback. Later on June 21, Channel 12 reported that Israel is considering limited pullbacks from parts of southern Lebanon including Beaufort, though senior officials said no formal U.S. withdrawal request had been received and stressed that staying on the border line is a red line.

items.title: Kerch Strait (near Kerch Bridge), Ukraine/Russia (disputed): Unverified claims indicated Ukraine's systematic targeting of logistical nodes, railway bridges, and air-defence systems around the peninsula is preparation for a massive siege of the Crimean Bridge.
items.description: Unverified claims indicated Ukraine's systematic targeting of logistical nodes, railway bridges, and air-defence systems around the peninsula is preparation for a massive siege of the Crimean Bridge.
items.rawSummary: Overnight Ukrainian drone strikes targeted fuel terminals, ferries, and air-defense systems near the Kerch Strait, causing a fire at an oil depot that burned into the late afternoon and further disrupting Russian supply routes to Crimea.
items.analysis: An overnight Ukrainian drone strike ignited a fire at an oil depot in occupied Kerch that continued burning into the late afternoon. Ukraine later announced it had struck targets on both sides of the Crimean Bridge, including oil transport infrastructure in Russia's Krasnodar region and the Kerch depot, and disabled four S-400 radar stations and two Pantsir air-defence systems. In parallel, three ferries carrying heavy vehicle traffic from the Russian mainland to Crimea were reported hit, compounding logistical disruption that forced fuel trucks to reroute via the R-280 road. Unverified claims suggest Ukraine may be preparing a massive siege of the bridge, with systematic targeting of logistical nodes, railway bridges, and air-defence systems around the peninsula. Russian authorities have not yet commented on the incidents, and Crimea remains under Russian control since 2014, a status not widely recognized internationally.

items.title: Geneva, Switzerland, Switzerland: Iran's delegation left the negotiation venue and returned to its Swiss residence, with talks continuing through intermediaries, Al-Arabiya reported.
items.description: Iran's delegation left the negotiation venue and returned to its Swiss residence, with talks continuing through intermediaries, Al-Arabiya reported.
items.rawSummary: US-Iran technical negotiations in Geneva progressed from a trilateral session into bilateral talks, with Iran's delegation departing the venue but discussions continuing through intermediaries, as Tehran maintained its nuclear program is not on the agenda and conditioned further progress on a Lebanon ceasefire.
items.analysis: After a one-day postponement, US-Iran technical negotiations began in Geneva with a trilateral meeting mediated by Qatar, Reuters reported; Vice President Vance described the talks as an effort to turn a 'new leaf' and the first direct US-Iran team session. Iran's earlier demand for Lebanon ceasefire guarantees led to the inclusion of Pakistan, but protocol tensions emerged when Iran refused a joint photo and handshake, canceling a media event, according to Tasnim. The initial trilateral session lasted 80 minutes and transitioned into bilateral Iran-Qatar talks, while Iran formally protested recent Trump statements and threatened to halt negotiations unless Israel ends Lebanon operations, per Iranian media. Iran insisted the nuclear program was not on the agenda, focusing instead on the ceasefire, sanctions relief, and frozen assets, consistent with a memorandum clause that ties final nuclear deal talks to the ceasefire's implementation. IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi was on hand for nuclear technical matters, even as Tehran denied nuclear issues were under discussion. Later, Iran's delegation left the negotiation venue and returned to its Swiss residence, with talks continuing through intermediaries, Al-Arabiya reported.

items.title: Belarus, Belarus: Zelenskyy threatens to remove relay transmitters in Belarus if Lukashenko does not do so within a week.
items.description: Zelenskyy threatens to remove relay transmitters in Belarus if Lukashenko does not do so within a week.
items.rawSummary: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy has set multiple one-week deadlines for Belarus to cease supporting Russia's war, threatening retaliation including the removal of relay transmitters, while accusing Minsk of supplying military components and fuel.
items.analysis: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has issued multiple one-week ultimatums to Belarus, first demanding a halt to Russian weapons launches from its territory and subsequently threatening to remove relay transmitters if President Lukashenko does not act. In a separate statement, he expanded on Belarus’s material support, alleging that Belarusian factories supply components for Russian armored vehicles and missile systems, and that fuel exports to Russia surged dramatically in early 2026. Zelenskyy has linked these actions to a deeper involvement in the conflict and warned of Ukrainian retaliation, including direct action against infrastructure. Belarus has not committed its own troops but remains a critical staging ground for Russian operations. The evolving demands signal a sharp escalation in rhetoric that now ties military, economic, and technical cooperation to the threat of cross-border Ukrainian action.
